# OpenTimestamps fixtures

Real proofs and real Bitcoin block headers used by `tests/test_anchor_ots.py`. Nothing here is
generated by this repository; the tests are offline and never fetch these again.

Retrieved 2026-11-16.

## Proofs

Source: <https://github.com/opentimestamps/opentimestamps-client/tree/master/examples>
(raw URL prefix `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opentimestamps/opentimestamps-client/master/examples/`).
The upstream repository is licensed LGPL-3.0; the `.ots` files are data files that this repository
only reads, never links or modifies. Each is checked by a byte-exact parse/serialize round trip.

### gdp2q25-2nd.pdf.ots

- File digest (SHA-256): `c70972a12908b73c2407d9cc6842ba2a02203a690f3090cd29f30c45f0cfd93d`
- Attests: Bitcoin block **912095** (2025, modern difficulty, about 2^78 work).
- Single attestation path, ops in order (tags): `prepend(99 B)` `append(35 B)` then repeated
  `sha256 sha256` pairs each preceded by an `append(32 B)` / `prepend(32 B)` step (Bitcoin
  transaction double-SHA-256 and merkle path), ending in the Bitcoin attestation. The message
  at the attestation equals the block header's merkle root.
- Does **not** use RIPEMD-160, so it verifies on every platform.

### hello-world.txt.ots

- File digest (SHA-256): `03ba204e50d126e4674c005e04d82e84c21366780af1f43bd54a37816b6ab340`
- Attests: Bitcoin block **358391** (2015, about 2^67 work, so the tests lower the work floor to
  60 for it; the production floor of 70 correctly refuses it). Block hash
  `000000000000000003e892881a8cdcdc117c06d444057c98b6f04a9ee75a2319`, merkle root
  `007ee445d23ad061af4a36b809501fab1ac4f2d7e7a739817dd0cbb7ec661b8a`.
- Single attestation path, ops in order (tags): **`ripemd160`** `prepend(200 B)` `append(6 B)`
  `sha256 sha256` then repeated `append/prepend(32 B)` + `sha256 sha256` pairs, ending in the
  Bitcoin attestation.
- **The first op is ripemd160 (RIPEMD-160), so this path needs `hashlib.new("ripemd160")`.**
  Some OpenSSL 3 builds lack it; the verification test skips there, and a separate test
  monkeypatches the helper to raise `UnsupportedOp` to prove the path is skipped and named in
  the verdict detail. The byte-exact round trip needs no hashing and runs everywhere.

### two-calendars.txt.ots

- File digest (SHA-256): `efaa174f68e59705757460f4f7d204bd2b535cfd194d9d945418732129404ddb`
- Attests: nothing on Bitcoin yet. Two **pending** calendar attestations,
  `https://alice.btc.calendar.opentimestamps.org` and `https://bob.btc.calendar.opentimestamps.org`.
- Both paths, ops in order: `append(16 B)` `sha256` `append(16 B)` `sha256` `prepend(4 B)`
  `append(8 B)`; the message at each pending node is 44 bytes, not 32.
- No ripemd160 anywhere, so it runs on every platform.

## Block headers (`headers.json`)

`{"<height>": {"hash": "<block hash, big-endian hex>", "header": "<80-byte header, hex>"}}` for
heights 912095 and 358391. For each height, `https://blockstream.info/api/block-height/{h}` and
`https://mempool.space/api/block-height/{h}` returned the same block hash, the header came from
`https://blockstream.info/api/block/{hash}/header`, and it double-SHA-256 hashes to that block hash.

## Calendar response

### calendar-pending.bin

- Captured 2026-11-16 from a live POST of 32 random bytes to
  `https://a.pool.opentimestamps.org/digest` (headers `Accept: application/vnd.opentimestamps.v1`
  and a User-Agent). HTTP 200, 242 bytes.
- Digest posted: `a58ef9f839009e86d1256d2528d97f9a98ed111b0de36abb99728418f9806927`.
- The body is a bare serialized timestamp (no file header) whose root message is the posted digest;
  it ends in a pending attestation (tag `83dfe30d2ef90c8e`) naming
  `https://alice.btc.calendar.opentimestamps.org`. It grounds the pending tag and the URI shape the
  allowlist in `fc/anchor.py` has to accept. Tests parse it against whatever digest they stamp; the
  structure, not the digest, is what matters.
